cards.text: Paul, called to be an apostle (Rom 1:1), writes to the church of the Thessalonians, in Thessalonica, a city in Macedonia (Acts 27:2). Silvanus and Timothy, who preached Christ with him (2 Cor 1:19), sign it too, which makes it a group project where everybody actually SHOWED UP. Paul opens by wishing them grace and peace.

cards.question: Paul tells the Thessalonians that he and his team thank God for them only now and then.

cards.text: When they pray, Paul and his team keep recalling three things before God: the Thessalonians' work of faith, their labor of love and their enduring hope. That's a GREAT way to be remembered, friend, because the last thing anybody remembered me for was being stuck behind the old takeout menus in that junk drawer.

cards.question: Paul remembers the Thessalonians' enduring hope. Who is that hope in?
Paul calls the Thessalonians brothers beloved by God and says he knows God has chosen them.

cards.text: So how does Paul know they're chosen? He points back to the day the gospel came to them, and it came with a whole lot more than just talk.

cards.question: Paul says the gospel came to the Thessalonians in word. What else does he say it came in?

cards.text: The Thessalonians saw how Paul's team lived among them, for their sake. Then they welcomed the message with the joy of the Holy Spirit, and that's not fresh-out-of-the-oven joy, friend, that's a WHOLE other level.

cards.question: The Thessalonians welcomed the message with joy, in spite of their great ___.
By welcoming the message that way, the Thessalonians became imitators of whom?
As a result, Paul says the Thessalonians became an ___ to all the believers in Macedonia and Achaia.

cards.text: The message of the Lord rang out from the Thessalonians to Macedonia and Achaia. That's my Mags all over, friend: one little bell, and the WHOLE kitchen stops to listen.

cards.question: Paul says news of the Thessalonians' faith in God stayed inside Macedonia and Achaia.
With the Thessalonians' faith known everywhere, what does Paul say his team has no need to do?

cards.text: Picture Paul starting to brag on them and everybody going, "Yeah, we HEARD." People report it themselves, including what kind of welcome the Thessalonians gave Paul's team.

cards.question: Those reports say the Thessalonians turned to God. What did they turn away from?

cards.text: They turned to serve the living and true God, and they're waiting too. I know waiting, friend, I did YEARS in a junk drawer, but nobody in there was waiting on anything this good.

cards.question: The Thessalonians are waiting for someone to come from heaven. Who is it?
God raised His Son from the dead, and Paul calls Him Jesus our deliverer from the coming ___.

findings.problem: "He points back to the day the gospel came to them" adds a single day. 1 Thessalonians 1:5 says only that the gospel came to them and gives no time.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: "By welcoming the message that way" makes the welcome the means of their imitation. 1 Thessalonians 1:6 says only that they became imitators "when" they welcomed the message, and it leaves the link open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the wording "coming wrath". Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason out wrath over famine or storm, so the card tests unseen wording, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
